beats.idea: Barter stalls when wants do not match
beats.shows: Grain refused; shoes stay; question mark between traders
beats.template_note: Buyer offers grain for shoes; at ask, seller shakes head and grain gets a cross on नहीं. Stop before swap; add question mark on कैसे.

beats.idea: Barter: wheat exchanged for cloth
nouns: 10 kg wheat in ten 1 kg portions
beats.shows: Two wheat portions swap for cloth; eight remain.
beats.template_note: Show ten 1 kg wheat portions; farmer offers two for the seller's 1 metre cloth. Exchange on देकर and लिया; retain eight wheat portions beside the farmer's received cloth. No money.

beats.idea: Barter में सीधा exchange, पैसा नहीं
beats.relation_note: दो लोगों के goods सीधे विपरीत दिशाओं में जाते हैं; बीच में money intermediary नहीं।
beats.shows: Wheat–cloth swap; crossed-out money beside direct arrows
beats.template_note: दो लोग wheat और cloth offer करके एक-दूसरे की चीज चाहते हैं और swap करते हैं; 'बिना' पर money icon पर cross आए।

beats.idea: पैसे से जुड़ी खरीद-बिक्री barter नहीं
beats.relation_note: पहले wheat बेचकर पैसा मिलता है; फिर वही पैसा अलग seller को देकर cloth मिलता है।
beats.shows: Wheat sale, money payment, cloth purchase; barter crossed
beats.template_note: तीन participants: wheat buyer पैसा देकर wheat लेता है; मूल wheat seller वही पैसा अलग cloth seller को देकर cloth लेता है। 'नहीं' पर barter label पर cross।

beats.idea: Barter की पहचान direct swap
beats.relation_note: सीधे goods swap पर tick देकर पहचान पक्की करें।
beats.shows: Direct wheat–cloth swap with a tick
beats.template_note: दोनों की चीजें बिना किसी money stop के सीधे swap हों; पूरे swap पर tick आए।

beats.idea: No money does not mean free
beats.relation_note: Contrast absent cash with actual payment in wheat.
beats.shows: Crossed money; wheat and cloth swap hands
beats.template_note: Wheat pays for cloth; no money changes hands.

beats.idea: Services can also be bartered
beats.relation_note: A repair service and grain move in opposite directions.
beats.shows: Bicycle repaired; grain handed to repair worker
beats.template_note: Worker repairs bicycle; owner gives grain in exchange.

beats.idea: Both parties decide the exchange value
beats.relation_note: Both parties approve the proposed quantities; neither decides alone.
beats.shows: Wheat–cloth question mark becomes two-party handshake
beats.template_note: Both examine the offered quantities, then both nod agreement.

beats.idea: One agreed ratio, not a universal rate
beats.relation_note: Pair the example quantities without implying a fixed market rate.
beats.shows: Example frame: 2 kg wheat ↔ 1 metre cloth
beats.template_note: Both approve and exchange these quantities; label the pair 'Example'.

beats.idea: Barter covers goods and services without money
beats.relation_note: Group goods-for-goods and service-for-goods examples under barter.
beats.shows: Barter box: wheat–cloth, repair–grain; crossed money outside
beats.template_note: This is a classification recap using completed exchanges, not a new transaction.

beats.idea: Direct exchange, no money, mutual consent
beats.relation_note: Both agree, then goods move directly between them without cash.
beats.shows: Two nods; direct wheat–cloth swap; crossed money
beats.template_note: Both nod at the offer, then exchange wheat and cloth directly.

beats.idea: Barter survives from early civilizations
beats.shows: Ancient barter crowd; arrow to neighbours swapping goods
beats.template_note: Neighbours offer grain and cloth, check mutual interest, then swap; timeline connects this with early barter.

beats.idea: Matching needs enable moneyless exchange
beats.shows: Matching needs ticked; grain and cloth swap hands
beats.template_note: Each neighbour wants the other's goods; matching thought bubbles receive ticks before the goods swap without money.

beats.idea: Money and barter coexist
beats.shows: Barter swap beside cash purchase; both remain visible
beats.template_note: Keep the completed barter exchange visible while a buyer hands money to a seller for vegetables in the adjacent scene.

beats.idea: Barter is less widespread today
beats.shows: Many early barter pairs; few present-day pairs
beats.template_note: Static prevalence comparison, not a new exchange process; pair counts are illustrative, not statistics.

beats.idea: जरूरत न मिले तो barter अस्वीकार
beats.relation_note: पहले seller की अस्वीकृति के बाद दूसरे की स्वीकृति दिखाएँ।
beats.shows: पहले wheat पर cross, फिर दूसरे संग अदला-बदली
beats.template_note: किसान wheat पेश करे; पहले seller के तेल वाले चाह-बुलबुले के सामने मना करता पर cross आए। दूसरा seller मान जाता पर tick दे; फिर 2 kg wheat और 1 metre कपड़ा बदलें।

beats.idea: दोनों की जरूरतों का मिलना जरूरी
beats.relation_note: एकतरफा जरूरत और दोतरफा जरूरत को समान दो-पक्षीय slots में दिखाएँ।
beats.shows: एकतरफा चाह असफल; दोतरफा चाह पर tick
beats.template_note: यह शर्त की व्याख्या है, नया लेनदेन नहीं; चाह के तीर और उनके सामने वस्तुएँ दिखें।

beats.idea: पैसा दो अलग सौदे जोड़ता है
beats.relation_note: पैसे की स्वीकृति wheat के खरीदार और cloth seller को अलग रखने देती है।
beats.shows: wheat बेचकर पैसा; पैसे देकर कपड़ा
beats.template_note: किसान wheat खरीदार को दे और पैसा ले; वही पैसा अलग cloth seller को देकर कपड़ा ले। दोनों पैसा स्वीकारें; cloth seller के चाह-बुलबुले में पैसा हो, wheat नहीं। रकम न लिखें।

beats.idea: अलग अनुपात और अविभाज्य गाय
beats.relation_note: ज्ञात wheat–cloth अनुपात के बाद गाय का अज्ञात अनुपात और छोटी खरीद की बाधा दिखाएँ।
beats.shows: wheat–कपड़ा अनुपात; साबुत गाय के पास प्रश्नचिह्न
beats.template_note: तय अनुपात और काल्पनिक विभाजन का प्रश्न है, सम्पन्न swap नहीं। गाय साबुत रहे; छोटी खरीद के सामने उसे बाँटने का प्रश्नचिह्न आए।

beats.idea: बाद का समान भुगतान, अलग विनिमय मूल्य
beats.relation_note: अभी लिया कपड़ा, भविष्य का अनाज-वादा, फिर लौटे अनाज की बदली क्रय-क्षमता।
beats.shows: अभी दो मीटर; बाद का अनाज एक मीटर
beats.template_note: Seller अभी 2 metres कपड़ा दे; रसीद पर तय quality का 10 kg अनाज बाद में देने का वादा दिखे। समय आगे बढ़े; borrower 10 kg अनाज लौटाए। अंतिम तुलना में यही अनाज अब केवल 1 metre कपड़े के बराबर दिखे; अतिरिक्त खरीद न दिखाएँ।

beats.idea: Barter की चार अलग कठिनाइयाँ
beats.shows: Ratios clash; cow indivisible; grain rots; repayment buys less
beats.template_note: Conceptual cause-effect panels, not a narrated transaction: reveal conflicting ratios, an undivided cow, spoiled grain, and equal repayment quantities with fewer goods later.

beats.idea: Money fixes debt units, not purchasing power
beats.shows: Fixed rupee debt; variable baskets; wants versus quantities
beats.template_note: Writing debt is mentioned as a convenience, not a cheque or transfer process. Show a rupee-denominated ledger beside different-sized goods baskets; separately contrast reciprocal wants with unresolved quantity scales.

beats.idea: Barter faces obstacles from matching through repayment
beats.shows: Matching, valuation, division, storage, repayment: obstacles throughout
beats.template_note: Summary of barriers, not an enacted swap: numbered arrow-linked stages show matching wants, agreeing quantities, indivisibility, storage and later repayment, each with a warning mark.

beats.idea: Barter first; payment methods evolve
beats.relation_note: Highlight the first stage, then trace the gallery’s arrows to establish changing payment methods.
beats.shows: Crossed coin; wheat–cloth swap; first stage highlighted
beats.template_note: Show wheat and cloth offered; a questioned coin between them receives a cross on ‘नहीं’. Exchange wheat directly for cloth on ‘barter’; highlight stage 1, then trace the gallery arrows on ‘बदलाव’.

beats.idea: Salt mediates two exchanges
beats.shows: Wheat swaps for salt; salt swaps for cloth
beats.template_note: Two consecutive swaps: farmer exchanges 2 kg wheat for 1 kg salt, then all that salt for 1 metre cloth. Keep salt visibly with the farmer between swaps; no eating.

beats.idea: Commodity money bridges buyers and sellers
beats.shows: Salt bridges exchange; cattle and shells join
beats.template_note: Explains the completed exchange rather than repeating it: salt occupies the bridge, wheat stays outside the cloth seller's receiving path. Reveal stage 2 COMMODITY MONEY with salt, cattle and shells.

beats.idea: Standard silver coins buy grain
beats.shows: Five coins; two paid; three remain; grain received
beats.template_note: Reveal five matching silver coins; buyer hands two to seller and receives 5 kg grain, leaving three. Matching weight and purity badges establish equivalence. Then reveal stage 3 METALLIC MONEY with gold and silver coins.

beats.idea: Countable coins also have material value
beats.shows: Counted coins sit inside commodity money grouping
beats.template_note: Reuse the two payment coins, counting them one by one without inventing a new total. Matching size, weight and purity markers show standardisation; a durability shield marks टिकाऊ. Nest gold and silver coins inside the commodity-money grouping at material value.

beats.idea: Notes pay at denomination and return change
beats.shows: ₹500 paid; goods received; ₹200 returned
beats.template_note: Show goods priced ₹300, ₹500 passing to seller, goods passing to buyer, and ₹200 returning. Reveal stage 4 PAPER MONEY. Highlight the note's ₹500 denomination; contrast with plain paper without assigning paper a price.

beats.idea: Notes reduce the burden of carrying value
beats.shows: Light note beside burdensome metal coin bag
beats.template_note: Static carrying-burden comparison, not a new payment: identical value markers above a light note and a heavy coin bag; no invented numerical amount.

beats.idea: A cheque transfers existing bank deposits
beats.shows: Cheque settles; buyer balance falls; seller balance rises
beats.template_note: Start buyer at ₹10,000 and seller at ₹2,000. Write ₹1,500 cheque, hand it to bank, then settle: buyer ₹10,000 → ₹8,500; seller ₹2,000 → ₹3,500. One connecting ₹1,500 transfer arrow prevents a money-creation impression. Reveal stage 5 BANK MONEY; highlight deposits as money and cheque as instruction.

beats.idea: Electronic instructions transfer deposit balances
beats.shows: Phone scans QR; balances shift by ₹300
beats.template_note: Begin a separate example at buyer ₹2,000 and seller ₹5,000. Phone visibly scans shop QR, shows ₹300 paid, and seller phone shows received. Update buyer to ₹1,700 and seller to ₹5,300 using one ₹300 transfer arrow. Reveal stage 6 DIGITAL MONEY with UPI phone, net-banking computer and card; electronic instruction travels, not paper.

beats.idea: Easier exchange; UPI transfers existing deposits
beats.shows: Money bridges exchange; UPI moves existing deposit tokens
beats.template_note: First show money bridging buyer and seller; on UPI, phone scans QR, then paid and received appear. Move identical deposit tokens from buyer account to seller account; combined tokens stay unchanged.

beats.idea: Forms coexist; cards need not store money
beats.shows: Coexisting forms; card linked to separate bank account
beats.template_note: This explains coexistence and card storage, not a card payment; use a static card-to-account link, without tapping.

beats.idea: Six forms in evolutionary order
beats.shows: Six numbered forms highlighted along the book’s arrows
beats.template_note: Historical ordering, not an enacted barter transaction; highlight each existing gallery panel on its spoken form.

beats.idea: Two different sources of value
beats.shows: Salt and note questioned, then exchanged for goods
beats.template_note: Two hypothetical payment examples: salt packet valued at ₹20 and ₹500 note; do not imply equal values.

beats.idea: Usefulness survives loss of monetary acceptance
beats.shows: Refused salt cooks; paper lacks ₹500 material worth
beats.template_note: Seller refuses salt as payment; retain salt's cooking use. Cross ₹500 only beside raw paper, not on the valid note; cross a redemption receipt separately.

beats.idea: Material value versus external backing
beats.shows: Gold material versus note with law and trust

beats.idea: Inherent worth is nonmonetary usefulness
beats.shows: Salt seasons food; valid note still buys goods
beats.template_note: Salt pours into a cooking pot. Contrast negligible raw-paper value with an intact valid note beside purchasable goods.

beats.idea: Commodity objects versus monetary claims
beats.shows: Commodity objects grouped opposite notes and bank claims
beats.template_note: Examples form two groups, not a numerical count. Link the balance to a bank and payment claim, not stored physical goods.

beats.idea: Acceptance depends on onward spending
beats.shows: Salt refused outside; rupees travel to next shop
beats.template_note: Outside seller refuses salt; then arrows show accepted rupees continuing to another shop, explaining the contrast.

beats.idea: Small payments and easy transport
beats.shows: Bulky commodities versus small coins; torn note crossed
beats.template_note: Static comparison of denomination-based small payments and transport burden; show a pre-torn note crossed out, not note-tearing as a payment method.

beats.idea: UPI moves an existing bank balance
beats.shows: Bullion opposite notes, balances and UPI transfer
beats.template_note: Scan the shop QR, show paid and received confirmations; connect UPI to bank balances without creating a separate UPI money pile or inventing an amount.

beats.idea: Separate legal, practical and durability properties
beats.shows: Law, onward spending, small payments, transport and durability
beats.template_note: Reveal paired property icons alongside corresponding table rows: stamped law beside debt settlement, onward-spending arrows, small denominations, light wallet, durable metal versus damaged paper and technology-dependent digital access.

beats.idea: Four misleading equivalences corrected
beats.shows: Prices fluctuate; redemption crossed; offline balance remains
beats.template_note: Four miniatures: fluctuating commodity price; backing distinct from gold redemption; coin face value distinct from material value; unavailable phone access beside an unchanged bank balance.

beats.idea: Useful commodities can still deteriorate
beats.shows: Use differs from money; illness and moisture damage
beats.template_note: Separate cooking usefulness from payment value; illness points to an unwell cow, moisture to spoiled salt. No transaction process is narrated.

beats.idea: Payment salt also has cooking value
beats.shows: Grain swaps for salt; salt seasons cooking pot
beats.template_note: Seller gives grain and receives exactly two salt packets; on ‘आगे न चलें’ onward exchange stops; on ‘खाना बनाएगा’ seller pours salt into a cooking pot.

beats.idea: Payment value plus independent usefulness
beats.shows: Same salt: payment pouch beside cooking pot
beats.template_note: Static paired uses establish the definition; no transaction sequence is narrated.

beats.idea: Neither usefulness nor purchasing power alone suffices
beats.shows: Salt: two ticks; note: commodity badge crossed
beats.template_note: Compare payment and non-payment-use slots. Reveal salt's usefulness tick first, payment tick at 'payment', and cross the note's commodity badge at 'नहीं'; no payment process is narrated.

beats.idea: Useful even outside payment
beats.shows: Payment salt beside salt seasoning food
beats.template_note: Two uses of the same commodity recap its defining property rather than narrating a process.

beats.idea: Salt regions versus cattle-keeping communities
beats.relation_note: Salt links to geographical regions; cattle link to a livelihood community, not a country.
beats.shows: Salt beside regions; cattle beside herding families
beats.template_note: Describes locations and livelihoods, not a transaction or counting process.

beats.idea: Cowries function through acceptance, not edibility
beats.relation_note: Connect cowries to India, China and Africa; an accepting recipient reinforces their monetary use.
beats.shows: Palm-held cowries, three regions, recipient nodding acceptance
beats.template_note: Show shells first; recipient nods and a tick appears on स्वीकार.

beats.idea: Tea bricks and tobacco have distinct regions
beats.relation_note: Pair compressed tea with Central Asia and Tibet, and dried tobacco leaves with Colonial America.
beats.shows: Tea brick and tobacco beside respective mapped regions
beats.image_wanted: compressed tea brick textured tea leaves; dried tobacco leaves
beats.template_note: Describes finished commodities and their regions; no manufacturing process is narrated.

beats.idea: Three quantities assumed equal in value
beats.shows: Farmer wants cloth; three equal-value goods alongside

beats.idea: Grain becomes salt, then cloth
beats.shows: Grain exchanged for salt, then salt for cloth
beats.template_note: Two consecutive swaps: farmer gives all 10 kg grain to salt trader and receives 2 kg salt; then gives all salt to cloth seller and receives 2 metres cloth. Show empty grain and salt sacks beside the farmer's final cloth.

beats.idea: Salt bridges unmatched wants
beats.relation_note: Onward acceptance lets the farmer accept salt without needing it personally.
beats.shows: Buyer’s salt reaches farmer, then cloth seller
beats.template_note: Two linked exchanges: buyer hands salt to farmer for produce; farmer passes salt to cloth seller for cloth. Keep buyer's cloth slot empty: no matching cloth offer is required.

beats.idea: Commodities also have direct uses
beats.relation_note: Group four commodity examples under uses beyond payment.
beats.shows: Salt seasons food; cattle, tea, tobacco serve needs
beats.template_note: Use paired object-and-use pictures, not transaction animation; the beat describes utility and demand.

beats.idea: Utility plus local acceptance enables commodity money
beats.relation_note: Join usefulness and community acceptance into easier exchange; add a secondary chronology before common metallic coins.
beats.shows: Utility plus local acceptance unlocks exchange before coins
beats.template_note: Barter becoming easier is a causal summary, not a specified swap. Show usefulness alone failing to unlock exchange, both conditions opening it within one community, and commodity money preceding common metallic coins.

beats.idea: Spoilage reduces grain available for future payment
beats.relation_note: Spoilage reduces stored grain from 100 kg to 90 kg, making future payment uncertain.
beats.shows: 100kg grain → 90kg usable → future payment question
beats.template_note: Show 100 kg stored grain; 10 kg visibly spoils, leaving 90 kg usable. Connect the reduced stock to a later calendar and an unresolved grain-payment arrow between payer and payee.

beats.idea: Commodity money has several practical limitations
beats.shows: Spoiled grain; cows and sacks beneath limitation symbols
beats.template_note: Names limitations; later beats demonstrate their mechanisms.

beats.idea: Variation and missing standards require repeated checks
beats.shows: Unequal cows; missing standards trigger weighing and bargaining
beats.template_note: Compare cows; show weight and quality rules, then their absence causing repeated weighing, inspection and bargaining.

beats.idea: Division, spoilage and hauling add costs
beats.shows: Indivisible cow, spoiled grain, hauling; arrows to costs
beats.template_note: Attempt a small payment with an intact cow; grain spoils in storage; porter struggles with sack; each branch adds expense coins. Do not depict cutting an animal.

beats.idea: Limitations differ across commodities
beats.shows: Grain divides, cow stays whole; shells outlast food
beats.template_note: Split grain into small portions while cow remains whole; contrast food spoiling with shells remaining unchanged.

beats.idea: Handling difficulties favour durable measured metal units
beats.shows: Matching tick; handling burdens point toward measured metal
beats.template_note: Concluding causal comparison, not a narrated transaction or manufacturing process.
